store.0: I've seen how the campus culture has evolved over the years as a fourth-year Computer Science student. There are many ways to get involved beyond coding.

I'm a Computer Science major, and I'm in my fourth year. My schedule this semester is really packed, but it's a good kind of busy. I'm finally taking the higher-level courses that I've been looking forward to for a while. It's surreal to think about how far I've come since my freshman year, when I was just learning about simple data structures. Now, I'm diving into complex algorithmic concepts, advanced system design, and even basic quantum computing. It's exciting to see how much I've grown and how much more I have to learn.

store.21: I'm a fourth-year computer science major with a passion for coding. My hobbies help me stay sane amidst a hectic schedule of classes and projects. I believe taking breaks and exploring outside interests can actually enhance my programming skills by providing a fresh perspective. It's essential to maintain a balance between work and play.
store.22: Sailing is a hobby that brings me a sense of freedom and helps me clear my mind. It's a unique activity that allows me to challenge myself and enjoy the thrill of the wind and water. I'm grateful to have had the opportunity to learn how to sail with my dad when I was younger, and I continue to enjoy it whenever I can. It's a great way to escape the stresses of college life and find some inner peace.
store.23: Regular gym workouts are a passion of mine that help me maintain a healthy lifestyle. It's a great way to offset the sedentary nature of coding and improve my overall well-being. I started with a basic lifting routine in college and have continued to develop my skills over the years. I enjoy seeing incremental improvements in my strength and energy levels, which motivates me to keep up the routine. Gym sessions are also a great stress-reliever after long coding sessions, and the mental clarity I gain from exercise helps me stay productive and sleep better.
store.24: Gaming is a hobby that complements my interest in technology and allows me to engage in problem-solving in a more relaxed environment. I enjoy playing co-op survival games, where I can gather resources, build shelters, and fend off creatures. It's a great way to challenge myself without the intensity of debugging code. I also appreciate the social aspect of gaming, as it allows me to connect with friends and classmates. Additionally, I've dabbled in game development using tools like Unity and Unreal Engine, which I hope to explore further in the future. Bridging the gap between playing games and creating them is fascinating, and I believe it can be a rewarding experience.
store.25: Reading has been a lifelong passion of mine, thanks to my mom's love of literature. She introduced me to fantasy and sci-fi novels when I was a kid, and I'd get lost in other worlds for hours. Even with a busy schedule, I try to squeeze in some reading before bed or on weekends. Lately, I've been fascinated by sci-fi novels that explore artificial intelligence, which aligns with my academic interests. I enjoy imagining future technology and the blurred boundaries between humans and machines. My current favorite AI-themed sci-fi book is 'The Infinity Courts' by Akemi Dawn Bowman. Reading books like this not only provides relaxation but also helps me explore philosophical questions about the work I'll be doing after graduation.
store.26: I've found that scheduling my hobbies helps me maintain a healthy balance between work and play. By planning ahead, I can ensure that I make time for activities like sailing, gym workouts, gaming, and reading. It's essential to prioritize self-care and relaxation to avoid burnout. I believe that having a variety of hobbies allows me to stay engaged and fulfilled, both academically and personally. By incorporating these activities into my routine, I can maintain a positive outlook and enjoy the college experience to the fullest.
store.27: I enjoy combining my hobbies to create unique experiences. For example, I've had a day where I spent the morning sailing at the lake, then grabbed lunch, and ended the day playing video games with friends. It was fascinating to see how the experience on the water was similar to coordinating movement in an online co-op. In both cases, everyone has a role to play, whether it's manning the sails or leading the in-game strategy. I love how each hobby demands teamwork, attention to detail, and problem-solving. It's great to see how different activities can complement each other and enhance my skills in various ways.
store.28: I believe that passion for hobbies is what drives us to make time for them, even with a busy schedule. It's not about doing everything at once, but rather finding small increments that work for us. For example, I might not be able to read for hours, but I can read one chapter. Similarly, I might not be able to sail every weekend, but once a month is better than nothing. And when it comes to gaming, even 30 minutes can be enough for a quick match. It's all about finding a balance and making the most of the time we have.
store.29: I believe that having a variety of hobbies allows me to showcase different aspects of myself and adds depth to my personality. It's wonderful to have something unique to talk about outside of coding, as it helps me connect with others on a different level. My hobbies range from the calming experience of reading to the thrilling sensation of sailing, from the discipline of weightlifting to the adrenaline rush of co-op games. This diversity makes life more interesting and fulfilling. I'm grateful for the opportunity to share my passion for hobbies with you.
store.30: I've been involved in undergraduate research since the end of my sophomore year, and it's been one of the most eye-opening parts of my college experience. It's given me a glimpse into how knowledge is created in the tech world, and it's pretty cool to be part of that. As a freshman, I didn't see myself going down the research route. I was into coding projects and hackathons, but I didn't think of research as 'my thing.' However, one of my professors, who taught an introductory data science class, noticed my ability to bridge technical coding with user experience. She suggested I apply for a research assistant position in a lab focused on data visualization for big scientific datasets. I was initially hesitant because research seemed intimidating, but I decided to take the leap. It turned out to be a great decision.
